audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart is blanket 'Skill' on rows 0-5 while the content layer and packet both give Xerath levels 1-6 and Veigar from first item on. Two layers disagreed on 6 of 7 rows. Content whys[4] also argued Veigar while win[4] says Xerath.
audit.why: Xerath's 750/1000/1050-range Q/W/E out-range Veigar's entire kit pre-item; Veigar flips from first item. Content win[] and packet agree.
audit.corrected: Full rows 0-5 aligned to the content layer with whys rewritten; content whys[4] softened to match Xerath holding the row.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text used 'Rite of the Ancients' — the ability is Rite of the Arcane.
audit.why: Kit file is authoritative on names.
audit.corrected: Name fixed in the spikes[1] rewrite.

audit.whatIsWrong: Missing interaction: Rite of the Arcane is a channel that roots Xerath — Event Horizon's stun cancels it outright. breakdown.cooldowns also carried no number.
audit.why: Kit flags R as channel-interruptible; Veigar E is hard CC. Shocking Orb E is 13s rank 1 / 11s max; R is 130s.
audit.corrected: Channel-cancel added to spikes[1], phases[4].why and breakdown.cooldowns; real cooldowns written in.

audit.why: Shocking Orb 13-11s is the lane's green light.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad bleed.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten grounded in Xerath's ranges.

audit.why: Nothing verifiable from kits; nothing asserted.

edits.before: Q through two units on every last-hit — each stack is permanent AP; the lane is a savings account from level 1.
edits.after: Xerath's Arcanopulse out-ranges your whole kit at level 1 — take safe last-hits only and eat no free poke.

edits.before: W on cage-stunned or rooted targets only — uncaged Dark Matter is a donation to his dodge stats.
edits.after: At 2 his Q-W poke zones you off the wave — hide behind casters and hold W for stunned targets.

edits.before: Cage online: drop it ON yourself when he engages, behind him when he farms — the geometry does the fighting.
edits.after: Cage online, but he out-ranges it by 300 units — drop it on yourself when the jungler shows, not to reach him.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-stack on cooldown and double-stack off cannon waves. The curve is the matchup.
edits.after: Through 4-5 his 1050-range Shocking Orb and artillery hold the lane — Q-stack safely and wait for 6.

edits.before: Primordial Burst online — anyone under half is now a math problem with one answer. Count R damage out loud.
edits.after: At 6 he still out-ranges you, but his R is a self-rooting channel — your cage cancels it and E-W-R kills him.

edits.before: Luden's spike: cage-W-Q-R deletes squishies who touch the wall. Your zone is a courtroom now.
edits.after: First item plus E rank: survive the poke and one-combo him when caged — his one stun is his only out.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Xerath wins by chipping you with 750-range Arcanopulse and W barrages until every step to farm costs health.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Event Horizon (self-cage) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb (E) is his only CC — 13s at rank 1, 11s max; dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill, and its downtime is your green light. - Rite of the Arcane (R, 130s) roots him in place and is a channel: your Event Horizon cancels the barrage outright.

edits.before: Cage his step-up, W the edge-stun, Q-auto, and walk — a half-bar trade that also deposited three stacks into the curve.
edits.after: He must step to 750 range for Arcanopulse — cage that step-up, W the edge-stun, and he has no dash to escape the combo.

edits.before: W-ing open ground on a moving target and trading uncaged 'just to stack' — Veigar without the wall is a piggy bank with a hat.
edits.after: Standing in a shove war inside his 1000-range W is exactly the poke he wants — take the stacks safe minions give, back off.

edits.before: At 6 you flip it — reach him once and E-W-R kills a champ with no self-peel.
edits.after: At 6 he still holds range, but reach him once and E-W-R kills him — bait the stun.

edits.before: Level 6 begins your comeback: Xerath's Rite of the Ancients (R) is pure long-range poke with no self-peel, so if you ever get on top of him a landed Event Horizon means W (Dark Matter) plus R kills him instantly. He has one Shocking Orb (E) stun to stop you — bait or dodge it and he's dead. Roam with your jungler to bridge the range gap since you can't walk him down in lane.
edits.after: Level 6 begins your comeback: Xerath's Rite of the Arcane (R) roots him in a channel your Event Horizon cancels outright, and it is pure poke with no self-peel — a landed cage means W (Dark Matter) plus R kills him instantly. He has one Shocking Orb (E) stun to stop you — bait or dodge it and he's dead. Roam with your jungler to bridge the range gap since you can't walk him down in lane.

notes: Level chart aligned: full rows 0-5 moved to match content win[] and the packet chart (which agree); content win[] untouched. Content whys[4] was rewritten because it argued Veigar flipping the row while win[4] holds Xerath. Suspect name 'Phenomenal Evil' in spikes[3] left alone — common shorthand for Veigar's passive (Riot: 'Phenomenal Evil Power'); the sentence is otherwise correct. Xerath is male; pronouns correct.
